title: Prime Agents hold a Right of First Refusal over each other's deployments, and forbearance is recorded in the Artifact
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.3 states that "Spark has formally agreed to the Ecosystem Accords herein," and A.6.1.1.1.3.3.1 names the first: an agreement with the Grove Agent, Ecosystem Accord 1. Underneath it sits a section whose only purpose is to log exercises of one clause — `Right of First Refusal Activity` (.1.1) — containing a single entry: "Spark **forwent** exercising its Right of First Refusal in order to enable Grove to deploy in Aave Core RLUSD" (.1.1.1).

Two things are established. First, Sky's Prime Agents are not independent actors competing freely: they hold contractual priority claims over each other's deployment opportunities, negotiated bilaterally and registered in both Artifacts. A ROFR means one Agent can pre-empt another's move into a venue or asset, which is a coordination device against Agents bidding against each other for the same allocations.

Second, and more unusual, *declining* to exercise the right is itself recorded as a Core provision. Most agreements log the exercise of an option; here the non-exercise gets a permanent numbered entry.

That asymmetry is the interesting part. Forbearance is the act that is otherwise invisible — an Agent that simply does nothing leaves no trace, and later cannot prove it yielded, nor be held to having yielded. Writing it down converts a passive non-action into an auditable concession with a beneficiary and a reason, which is what makes reciprocity possible between Agents over time. It also makes the inter-Agent relationship legible to SPK holders, who can see what their Agent gave up and for whom.
description: Ecosystem Accord 1 gives Spark a ROFR against Grove; Spark's decision to forgo it so Grove could deploy in Aave Core RLUSD is logged as its own Core provision.
